1	> Default Generate also loads [`executor-base.md`](./executor-base.md); a selected chart-family SVG is adapted through [`executor-visualization.md`](./executor-visualization.md), while native readiness and metadata remain exclusively in [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md).
2	
3	# Executor Chart Branch
4	
5	Conditional Executor authority for value-driven SVG geometry, plot-area markers, and the [`verify-charts`](../workflows/stages/verify-charts.md) handoff.
6	
7	**Trigger**: source values determine visible geometry — bar length/height, point position, arc angle, polygon vertex, connector or flow width/path, bubble center/radius, duration position, area, or another quantitative visual variable. Mini charts, sparklines, insets, and small multiples count even without a catalog reference.
8	
9	| Information model | Route |
10	|---|---|
11	| Values, dates, or durations determine geometry or another visual variable | This branch |
12	| Qualitative order, grouping, containment, causality, or named zones determine topology | [`executor-structure.md`](./executor-structure.md) |
13	| A row header and column header jointly address each body fact | [`executor-table.md`](./executor-table.md) |
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. Value-driven Geometry
18	
19	**Hard rule — data owns the marks**: derive every quantitative mark from the authoritative values and one explicit scale/encoding. Do not eyeball positions, preserve sample values from a catalog preview, or alter data to improve composition. A schedule is a Gantt chart when dates or durations determine each task bar's `x` and `width`, even if the source was a PowerPoint table; a qualitative stage × lane placement belongs to `executor-structure.md`.
20	
21	Construct in this order: (1) resolve data domain, categories, units, baseline, scale, and any radius/color/bin mapping; (2) establish the plot frame, axes/grid or radial frame, and legend needed to decode them; (3) calculate marks from the values, including cumulative, derived, or hierarchical geometry; (4) add data labels, axis/category labels, annotations, units, source notes, and visible exceptions from the page contract; (5) apply project typography, palette, effects, and container treatment without changing the encoding.
22	
23	**Perceptual reading**: choose the least ambiguous presentation of the same data. Preserve source or semantic order when it carries meaning; otherwise sort for the page's comparison task; a right-to-left deck sets `axes.category.reverse` so categories read the way the page does. Prefer direct series labels when legible; keep legends, grid lines, and ticks only when they materially reduce lookup effort. Comparable panels share domain, scale, and category order unless a disclosed difference is the message. Magnitude bars and columns start from zero; interval marks keep their authoritative domain; any non-zero baseline or axis break is explicit and never exaggerates. A dual-axis chart is valid only when both series share the exact time/category domain and units and identities stay unambiguous; otherwise separate the views.
24	
25	**Reference — chart color and annotation conventions**: a monochromatic depth scheme reads cleaner than rainbow — the primary series in the full theme color, a comparison series in the same hue at about 60% alpha, baselines as a gray dashed line (solid and lighter on a native-marked chart, whose series carry no dash), the accent color only on the key data points; positive / warning / negative trends use the deck's green / yellow / red polarity roles. Place direct data labels at bar ends or beside points instead of a legend where they stay legible; annotate genuine inflection points in words ("policy change", "product launch"); mark an industry average or target as a gray dashed comparison baseline; keep units and precision consistent within one chart; add a muted source note where attribution or provenance matters.
26	
27	**Per-object completeness**: preserve every authoritative series, category, point, label, unit, qualifier, source, and scale cue. For a `<object-key>=yes` chart, the JSON mirrors the drawn fallback item by item in the same edit — legend labels verbatim, point-level exception colors as `point_colors`, the axis scale, `plot_area` from the plot-area marker, visible data labels or summary figures as `data_labels` or companion text, actual label/axis/grid colors (omit `text_color` and siblings rather than guess). When the source cannot determine a required scale or derived value, return the ambiguity upstream in Default or resolve it from explicit source facts in Quick; never fabricate at draw time.
28	
29	**Selected reference**: with a `chart/<key>` primary reference, [`executor-visualization.md`](./executor-visualization.md) owns resolution and adaptation; this branch still owns the value-to-geometry calculation. A chart authored from scratch follows the same contract. An incidental microvisual (small trend or indicator) is drawn accurately but enters §2 and verification only when Default §IX or the Quick active-context decision promotes it to a coordinate-verified object.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Plot-area Marker
34	
35	### 2.1 Chart Plot-Area Marker (Mandatory per verified chart object)
36	
37	**Hard rule — object-scoped marker**: every Default chart object keyed in §IX `Visualization`, and every Quick chart object promoted for coordinate verification, has one page-local `kebab-case` object key. Wrap it in `<g id="<object-key>">`; place exactly one marker inside its plot-area group `id="<object-key>-chartArea"`, after the axes and before the first data mark, with payload prefix `object=<object-key> |`. A legacy unscoped marker with `<g id="chartArea">` is accepted only when the page has exactly one verified chart object.
38	
39	```xml
40	<g id="revenue-trend">
41	  <g id="revenue-trend-chartArea">
42	    <!-- axes -->
43	    <!-- chart-plot-area: object=revenue-trend | x_min,y_min,x_max,y_max -->
44	    <!-- data marks -->
45	  </g>
46	</g>
47	```
48	
49	```xml

> Default Generate also loads [`executor-base.md`](./executor-base.md); a selected chart-family SVG is adapted through [`executor-visualization.md`](./executor-visualization.md), while native readiness and metadata remain exclusively in [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md).

# Executor Chart Branch

Conditional Executor authority for value-driven SVG geometry, plot-area markers, and the [`verify-charts`](../workflows/stages/verify-charts.md) handoff.

**Trigger**: source values determine visible geometry — bar length/height, point position, arc angle, polygon vertex, connector or flow width/path, bubble center/radius, duration position, area, or another quantitative visual variable. Mini charts, sparklines, insets, and small multiples count even without a catalog reference.

| Information model | Route |
|---|---|
| Values, dates, or durations determine geometry or another visual variable | This branch |
| Qualitative order, grouping, containment, causality, or named zones determine topology | [`executor-structure.md`](./executor-structure.md) |
| A row header and column header jointly address each body fact | [`executor-table.md`](./executor-table.md) |

---

## 1. Value-driven Geometry

**Hard rule — data owns the marks**: derive every quantitative mark from the authoritative values and one explicit scale/encoding. Do not eyeball positions, preserve sample values from a catalog preview, or alter data to improve composition. A schedule is a Gantt chart when dates or durations determine each task bar's `x` and `width`, even if the source was a PowerPoint table; a qualitative stage × lane placement belongs to `executor-structure.md`.

Construct in this order: (1) resolve data domain, categories, units, baseline, scale, and any radius/color/bin mapping; (2) establish the plot frame, axes/grid or radial frame, and legend needed to decode them; (3) calculate marks from the values, including cumulative, derived, or hierarchical geometry; (4) add data labels, axis/category labels, annotations, units, source notes, and visible exceptions from the page contract; (5) apply project typography, palette, effects, and container treatment without changing the encoding.

**Perceptual reading**: choose the least ambiguous presentation of the same data. Preserve source or semantic order when it carries meaning; otherwise sort for the page's comparison task; a right-to-left deck sets `axes.category.reverse` so categories read the way the page does. Prefer direct series labels when legible; keep legends, grid lines, and ticks only when they materially reduce lookup effort. Comparable panels share domain, scale, and category order unless a disclosed difference is the message. Magnitude bars and columns start from zero; interval marks keep their authoritative domain; any non-zero baseline or axis break is explicit and never exaggerates. A dual-axis chart is valid only when both series share the exact time/category domain and units and identities stay unambiguous; otherwise separate the views.

**Reference — chart color and annotation conventions**: a monochromatic depth scheme reads cleaner than rainbow — the primary series in the full theme color, a comparison series in the same hue at about 60% alpha, baselines as a gray dashed line (solid and lighter on a native-marked chart, whose series carry no dash), the accent color only on the key data points; positive / warning / negative trends use the deck's green / yellow / red polarity roles. Place direct data labels at bar ends or beside points instead of a legend where they stay legible; annotate genuine inflection points in words ("policy change", "product launch"); mark an industry average or target as a gray dashed comparison baseline; keep units and precision consistent within one chart; add a muted source note where attribution or provenance matters.

**Per-object completeness**: preserve every authoritative series, category, point, label, unit, qualifier, source, and scale cue. For a `<object-key>=yes` chart, the JSON mirrors the drawn fallback item by item in the same edit — legend labels verbatim, point-level exception colors as `point_colors`, the axis scale, `plot_area` from the plot-area marker, visible data labels or summary figures as `data_labels` or companion text, actual label/axis/grid colors (omit `text_color` and siblings rather than guess). When the source cannot determine a required scale or derived value, return the ambiguity upstream in Default or resolve it from explicit source facts in Quick; never fabricate at draw time.

**Selected reference**: with a `chart/<key>` primary reference, [`executor-visualization.md`](./executor-visualization.md) owns resolution and adaptation; this branch still owns the value-to-geometry calculation. A chart authored from scratch follows the same contract. An incidental microvisual (small trend or indicator) is drawn accurately but enters §2 and verification only when Default §IX or the Quick active-context decision promotes it to a coordinate-verified object.

---

## 2. Plot-area Marker

### 2.1 Chart Plot-Area Marker (Mandatory per verified chart object)

**Hard rule — object-scoped marker**: every Default chart object keyed in §IX `Visualization`, and every Quick chart object promoted for coordinate verification, has one page-local `kebab-case` object key. Wrap it in `<g id="<object-key>">`; place exactly one marker inside its plot-area group `id="<object-key>-chartArea"`, after the axes and before the first data mark, with payload prefix `object=<object-key> |`. A legacy unscoped marker with `<g id="chartArea">` is accepted only when the page has exactly one verified chart object.

```xml
<g id="revenue-trend">
  <g id="revenue-trend-chartArea">
    <!-- axes -->
    <!-- chart-plot-area: object=revenue-trend | x_min,y_min,x_max,y_max -->
    <!-- data marks -->
  </g>
</g>
```

```xml
<!-- chart-plot-area: object=share-pie | pie | center: cx,cy | radius: r -->
<!-- chart-plot-area: object=share-donut | donut | center: cx,cy | outer-radius: r1 | inner-radius: r2 -->
<!-- chart-plot-area: object=capability-radar | radar | center: cx,cy | radius: r -->
```

| Value | Derivation |
|---|---|
| `x_min` / `x_max` | X of the Y-axis line or leftmost data boundary / rightmost axis endpoint or data boundary |
| `y_min` / `y_max` | Y of the topmost grid line or data boundary / X-axis baseline or bottom data boundary |
| `cx, cy` | Absolute center after containing translate transforms |
| `r`, `r1`, `r2` | Visible outer/inner radii of the authored radial geometry |

Calculator-supported SVGs in `templates/charts/` carry the same comment. A qualitative structure or cell-grid table gains no marker merely because it contains numbers. A missing marker invokes the verify stage's declared fallback and adds avoidable derivation work.

### 2.2 Authoring-time Check

After each page containing verified charts: `rg -n "chart-plot-area" <project_path>/svg_output/<current_page>.svg` — marker count equals promoted chart objects and each marker sits under its object wrapper.

**Native layout handoff**: for a native-ready classic chart whose authored plot rectangle must stay fixed, copy that absolute rectangle into metadata `plot_area`; omit it for PowerPoint automatic layout. The comment alone does not affect export; the closed schema is [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md) §2.

---

**ChartEx** (`waterfall`, `funnel`, `histogram`, `pareto`, `treemap`, `sunburst`, `box_whisker`) takes no `axes`, `plot_area`, or `data_labels`; values travel only as companion text — one `notes[]` entry per drawn value label, no tick labels — or pick a classic type.

## 3. Verification Handoff

Coordinate calibration is a conditional post-generation stage. After all SVG pages exist, run [`verify-charts`](../workflows/stages/verify-charts.md) whenever the active profile declares at least one page with value-driven chart geometry: Default enumerates Design Spec §IX (with the stage's legacy §VII fallback); Quick cross-checks still-active page decisions one-for-one against plot-area markers. Do not run `svg_position_calculator.py` during the initial draft; the stage calibrates completed geometry against the declared plot area, repairs genuine mismatches, and returns to the profile's checker order.

Distinguish header/body/summary with the lightest sufficient weight, fill, rule, and whitespace; decorative card treatment must not break row or column continuity. **Reference — table defaults (treatment follows the locked style)**: a header set apart by weight and a rule, or by a fill with reversed text where the style carries fills; zebra rows at `fill-opacity` 0.05, numbers right-aligned and text left-aligned with consistent units and precision, one highlighted row in the accent at `fill-opacity` 0.1, and horizontal rules only — avoid a full grid of lines (a native-marked table projects them as per-cell `borders`; a uniform payload border means a full grid).

1	> See [`executor-base.md`](./executor-base.md) for page authoring and [`shared-standards-core.md`](./shared-standards-core.md) for the mandatory SVG foundation and object-local authority boundary.
2	
3	# Native Data Interface
4	
5	Sole conditional interface for preset pattern fills and PowerPoint-native chart/table replacement — eligibility, markers, metadata schemas, and export activation. Load only when either feature is selected for the authored SVG. Import-side normalization and the closed PPTX import boundaries live in [`conversion.md`](../scripts/docs/conversion.md#native-table-and-chart-import-claims).
6	
7	## 1. Pattern Fill — `<pattern>` with PPTX preset annotation
8	
9	A `<pattern>` requests one fixed DrawingML preset; the converter never renders the tile's own geometry. Write `data-pptx-pattern="<preset>"` from the closed enum below (absent annotation falls back to `ltUpDiag` with a fidelity warning; an invalid name is an error because PowerPoint opens the file as "needs to be repaired"). Colors come from `data-pptx-fg` / `data-pptx-bg` or the pattern's child paint — the first child `<rect>` fill is the background (default white) and the first stroke or other fill the foreground (required). `patternTransform` is an error.
10	
11	| Category | Values |
12	|---|---|
13	| Grids | `smGrid` · `lgGrid` · `dotGrid` *(no `ltGrid`)* |
14	| Diagonal lines | `ltUpDiag` · `ltDnDiag` · `dkUpDiag` · `dkDnDiag` · `wdUpDiag` · `wdDnDiag` · `dashUpDiag` · `dashDnDiag` · `diagCross` |
15	| Horizontal / vertical lines | `horz` · `vert` · `ltHorz` · `ltVert` · `dkHorz` · `dkVert` · `narHorz` · `narVert` · `dashHorz` · `dashVert` · `cross` |
16	| Percent fills | `pct5` · `pct10` · `pct20` · `pct25` · `pct30` · `pct40` · `pct50` · `pct60` · `pct70` · `pct75` · `pct80` · `pct90` |
17	| Checks & confetti | `smCheck` · `lgCheck` · `smConfetti` · `lgConfetti` |
18	| Decorative | `horzBrick` · `diagBrick` · `weave` · `plaid` · `trellis` · `zigZag` · `wave` · `sphere` · `divot` · `shingle` · `solidDmnd` · `openDmnd` · `dotDmnd` |
19	
20	## 2. PowerPoint-Native Chart / Table Replacement Markers (Opt-in)
21	
22	The complete visible SVG fallback stays required for preview and default export; Chart/Table authority is object-local:
23	
24	- **SVG-first (default)** — free-design, Brand-only, and Style-only authoring omits `data-pptx-native-authority`; the visible subtree is the design authority and JSON its derived projection. Canonical authoring records `data-pptx-fallback-sha256` only after fallback and JSON are synchronized; a later visible edit regenerates the JSON and re-stamps. A missing or stale baseline keeps fallback export available but makes `--native-charts-and-tables` fail closed.
25	- **JSON-first (template / native source)** — a validated PPTX import or template-owned object writes `data-pptx-native-authority="json"`; inline JSON is the authority and the visible subtree an approximate derived preview regenerated from it. Legal only on active `chart` / `table` replacement groups.
26	
27	Both keep the JSON inside the SVG; `native_payloads.json.gz` is for opaque shape restoration only.
28	
29	**Hard rule — selected-object authoring**: write the marker and JSON for every supported chart and pure text-grid table in the same edit — both are native-ready by default, and an unactivated marker changes no export, so never skip an eligible object. Default reads the key from §IX `Native-ready: <object-key>=yes|no; …`; Quick assigns the same page-local `kebab-case` key before drawing; the key is the marker group `id` and metadata `name`. A catalog `family/key`, §VII row, numeric content, or another ready object never implies eligibility; `=no` entries and incidental microvisuals stay on the fallback route; a legacy bare `Native-ready: yes|no` maps only to the page's sole eligible object. **MUST — atomic authoring**: one object's visible fallback, `data-pptx-replace-with` marker, and single JSON `<metadata>` child are one authoring unit written while the data is in context, never deferred to `verify-charts`, the final gate, or export. Then stamp SVG-first objects:
30	
31	```bash
32	python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/stamp_native_fallbacks.py "<svg-file-or-directory>" --write   # read-only without --write; skips JSON-first
33	```
34	
35	The hash is a synchronization receipt, not proof of semantic equivalence; never stamp stale JSON to satisfy validation.
36	
37	**Hard rule — activation is the opt-in**: a marker only declares eligibility. Normal `svg_to_pptx.py` converts the fallback children into editable DrawingML shapes (a structured `chart` / `table` placeholder slot has no shape path and needs the flag); `--native-charts-and-tables` emits the PowerPoint Chart/Table object and discards the fallback children, so everything the fallback shows lives in the payload — data, point emphasis, line/area treatment, spacing, chrome, and companion text — and the final checker's parity findings block that export until they do. A convertible marker stays even when a detail has no native field: it becomes companion text or an unmarked sibling object, never a simpler drawing.
38	
39	| Replacement marker | Native output | Required metadata |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| `<g data-pptx-replace-with="table">` | `<p:graphicFrame>` with `<a:tbl>` | bounds + `columns` or `rows` |
42	| `<g data-pptx-replace-with="chart">` | `<p:graphicFrame>` with `c:chart` / `cx:chart` + chart part + embedded workbook | bounds + `type`, plus chart data |
43	
44	**Metadata placement and bounds**: one child `<metadata type="application/json">`; the marker's `data-pptx-replace-with` selects the schema. Provide `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` in metadata or as `data-pptx-x/y/width/height` on the group (complete explicit bounds are absolute slide coordinates; omitted bounds are inferred from the fallback geometry); JSON-first markers require all four in metadata. Classic charts accept a root `plot_area` rectangle inside the frame. Ranges, read-compatible spellings, and what the checker validates: [`native-data.md`](../scripts/docs/native-data.md).
45	
46	```xml
47	<g id="p03-revenue-chart" data-pptx-replace-with="chart">
48	  <metadata type="application/json">
49	    {
50	      "x": 120, "y": 150, "width": 520, "height": 320,
51	      "name": "p03-revenue-chart",
52	      "type": "column",
53	      "title": "Revenue by Segment",
54	      "categories": ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3"],
55	      "series": [
56	        {"name": "Cloud", "values": [12, 15, 19]},
57	        {"name": "Services", "values": [8, 9, 11]}
58	      ]
59	    }
60	  </metadata>
61	  <!-- Visible SVG fallback for live preview / non-native export goes here. -->
62	</g>
63	```
64	
65	**Hard rule — project by the selected authority**: SVG-first metadata describes the same data and visible chrome as its fallback — for a chart every category/point and series value (`null` for a break in a line), x/y/size data, visible point colors and markers (`line_style` / `point_colors`), line/area treatment (a line over a translucent fill is a `combo` of an area plot and a line plot), title/axis/legend chrome, companion text, bounds, and typography native export cannot infer; bar categories follow payload order top-down, and bar spacing, clustered overlap, and where a line starts inside `plot_area` are read from the fallback; for a table every resolved cell, header/summary line, rectangular span, cell style, alignment, bounds, and typography. JSON-first metadata is the authority and its preview may be approximate. Never simplify the artwork to fit the payload: when the closed payload cannot carry required data or topology, Default returns the native-ready decision upstream and Quick revises it before drawing; only the resolved non-native object stays unmarked, and an explicit `=yes` is never silently ignored. **Per-page verification**: every `=yes` key matches exactly one marker with one JSON child, and `=no` / unlisted objects have none — `rg -n 'data-pptx-replace-with="(chart|table)"|<metadata type="application/json">' <project_path>/svg_output/<current_page>.svg`.
66	
67	### Table schema — `ppt-master.semantic-table.v2`
68	
69	Every payload carries that exact `schema`; `columns` holds the optional header row and `rows` the body rows; `column_widths` / `row_heights` are relative weights. A cell is a string or an object with `text` (or `paragraphs` for rich text), `fill`, `color`, `align` (`l` / `ctr` / `r`), `valign` (`top` / `middle` / `bottom`), `bold`, `font_size`, `padding`, and per-side `borders` keyed `left` / `right` / `top` / `bottom` / `diagonal_down` / `diagonal_up` (full words, unlike `align`; each side is `{"style": "none"}` or `{"style": "solid", "color", "width"}`; a border without `style` is rejected); exact repetition may be factored into `defaults.cell` / `defaults.paragraph` / `defaults.run` (cell fields such as `align`, `valign`, `padding`, `font_size`, `borders` go under `defaults.cell`, never directly under `defaults`) and named `cell_styles`. Merged cells use positive `row_span` / `col_span` on the anchor with every covered cell as `{"merge_continuation": true}`. The complete field grammar: [`native-data.md`](../scripts/docs/native-data.md).
70	
71	**Hard rule — the table payload is complete**: every row, summary line, value, and cell style that must survive `--native-charts-and-tables` is in `columns` / `rows`, because fallback text is discarded on that route. A payload holding only `font_size` and a uniform border is not complete when the fallback draws a header band, row or column fills, first-column emphasis, non-uniform row heights, or sparse rules. Numeric or currency columns use cell objects with `align: "r"` (`text-anchor="end"` does not carry).
72	
73	### Chart schemas
74	
75	Supported `type` values: `column`, `bar`, `line`, `area` (each with `grouping`), `pie`, `doughnut`, `pieOfPie`, `barOfPie`, `radar`, `radarMarkers`, `radarFilled`, `scatter`, `bubble`, `combo`, `treemap`, `sunburst`, `histogram`, `pareto`, `boxWhisker`, `waterfall`, `funnel`, `stock`. Category charts take `categories` plus `series[].values`; XY charts take `series[].x` / `y` (bubble adds `size`); combo takes `plots[]` or typed `series[]`; ChartEx types take their own hierarchy or value fields. `data_labels` (column / bar / line / area plots only; other types show values through companion text), `axes` (per axis `minimum` / `maximum` / `major_unit`, never `min` / `max`), `axis_titles`, `show_legend` / `legend_position`, companion text (`caption`, `source`, `note`), and `style.colors` are the chrome fields. 3D aliases and `surface` are unsupported; exploded pie, `map`, `heatmap`, `bullet`, and `gantt` fail fast. A PPTX import spells `pieOfPie` / `barOfPie` as `of_pie` plus `of_pie_type`; keep the imported spelling when editing, and note the second plot's split is not a JSON field. Every field, enum, and range: [`native-data.md`](../scripts/docs/native-data.md).
76	
77	**Chart chrome and color**: SVG-first metadata matches the fallback chrome and reads it literally — the dominant stroke of elements named `axis` becomes `style.axis_color` and of those named `grid` becomes `style.grid_color` (unlabeled lines fall back to the marker's dominant stroke), numbers keep their written form (a payload `73.0` renders as `73` unless `number_format` says otherwise), and marker text that is not a category, data label, axis label, or legend entry needs a companion entry; JSON-first owns its chrome. Generated payloads use uppercase `#RRGGBB`. Negative bars keep the series fill. The final checker tags SVG-first parity findings `blocks --native-charts-and-tables export`; that export refuses them, so clear them before exporting the native variant.
78	
79	**Forbidden — replacement marker transforms**: no rotate, skew, or matrix on table/chart groups; translate/scale only, because native frames cannot carry arbitrary SVG transforms.

> See [`executor-base.md`](./executor-base.md) for page authoring and [`shared-standards-core.md`](./shared-standards-core.md) for the mandatory SVG foundation and object-local authority boundary.

# Native Data Interface

Sole conditional interface for preset pattern fills and PowerPoint-native chart/table replacement — eligibility, markers, metadata schemas, and export activation. Load only when either feature is selected for the authored SVG. Import-side normalization and the closed PPTX import boundaries live in [`conversion.md`](../scripts/docs/conversion.md#native-table-and-chart-import-claims).

## 1. Pattern Fill — `<pattern>` with PPTX preset annotation

A `<pattern>` requests one fixed DrawingML preset; the converter never renders the tile's own geometry. Write `data-pptx-pattern="<preset>"` from the closed enum below (absent annotation falls back to `ltUpDiag` with a fidelity warning; an invalid name is an error because PowerPoint opens the file as "needs to be repaired"). Colors come from `data-pptx-fg` / `data-pptx-bg` or the pattern's child paint — the first child `<rect>` fill is the background (default white) and the first stroke or other fill the foreground (required). `patternTransform` is an error.

| Category | Values |
|---|---|
| Grids | `smGrid` · `lgGrid` · `dotGrid` *(no `ltGrid`)* |
| Diagonal lines | `ltUpDiag` · `ltDnDiag` · `dkUpDiag` · `dkDnDiag` · `wdUpDiag` · `wdDnDiag` · `dashUpDiag` · `dashDnDiag` · `diagCross` |
| Horizontal / vertical lines | `horz` · `vert` · `ltHorz` · `ltVert` · `dkHorz` · `dkVert` · `narHorz` · `narVert` · `dashHorz` · `dashVert` · `cross` |
| Percent fills | `pct5` · `pct10` · `pct20` · `pct25` · `pct30` · `pct40` · `pct50` · `pct60` · `pct70` · `pct75` · `pct80` · `pct90` |
| Checks & confetti | `smCheck` · `lgCheck` · `smConfetti` · `lgConfetti` |
| Decorative | `horzBrick` · `diagBrick` · `weave` · `plaid` · `trellis` · `zigZag` · `wave` · `sphere` · `divot` · `shingle` · `solidDmnd` · `openDmnd` · `dotDmnd` |

## 2. PowerPoint-Native Chart / Table Replacement Markers (Opt-in)

The complete visible SVG fallback stays required for preview and default export; Chart/Table authority is object-local:

- **SVG-first (default)** — free-design, Brand-only, and Style-only authoring omits `data-pptx-native-authority`; the visible subtree is the design authority and JSON its derived projection. Canonical authoring records `data-pptx-fallback-sha256` only after fallback and JSON are synchronized; a later visible edit regenerates the JSON and re-stamps. A missing or stale baseline keeps fallback export available but makes `--native-charts-and-tables` fail closed.
- **JSON-first (template / native source)** — a validated PPTX import or template-owned object writes `data-pptx-native-authority="json"`; inline JSON is the authority and the visible subtree an approximate derived preview regenerated from it. Legal only on active `chart` / `table` replacement groups.

Both keep the JSON inside the SVG; `native_payloads.json.gz` is for opaque shape restoration only.

**Hard rule — selected-object authoring**: write the marker and JSON for every supported chart and pure text-grid table in the same edit — both are native-ready by default, and an unactivated marker changes no export, so never skip an eligible object. Default reads the key from §IX `Native-ready: <object-key>=yes|no; …`; Quick assigns the same page-local `kebab-case` key before drawing; the key is the marker group `id` and metadata `name`. A catalog `family/key`, §VII row, numeric content, or another ready object never implies eligibility; `=no` entries and incidental microvisuals stay on the fallback route; a legacy bare `Native-ready: yes|no` maps only to the page's sole eligible object. **MUST — atomic authoring**: one object's visible fallback, `data-pptx-replace-with` marker, and single JSON `<metadata>` child are one authoring unit written while the data is in context, never deferred to `verify-charts`, the final gate, or export. Then stamp SVG-first objects:

```bash
python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/stamp_native_fallbacks.py "<svg-file-or-directory>" --write   # read-only without --write; skips JSON-first
```

The hash is a synchronization receipt, not proof of semantic equivalence; never stamp stale JSON to satisfy validation.

**Hard rule — activation is the opt-in**: a marker only declares eligibility. Normal `svg_to_pptx.py` converts the fallback children into editable DrawingML shapes (a structured `chart` / `table` placeholder slot has no shape path and needs the flag); `--native-charts-and-tables` emits the PowerPoint Chart/Table object and discards the fallback children, so everything the fallback shows lives in the payload — data, point emphasis, line/area treatment, spacing, chrome, and companion text — and the final checker's parity findings block that export until they do. A convertible marker stays even when a detail has no native field: it becomes companion text or an unmarked sibling object, never a simpler drawing.

| Replacement marker | Native output | Required metadata |
|---|---|---|
| `<g data-pptx-replace-with="table">` | `<p:graphicFrame>` with `<a:tbl>` | bounds + `columns` or `rows` |
| `<g data-pptx-replace-with="chart">` | `<p:graphicFrame>` with `c:chart` / `cx:chart` + chart part + embedded workbook | bounds + `type`, plus chart data |

**Metadata placement and bounds**: one child `<metadata type="application/json">`; the marker's `data-pptx-replace-with` selects the schema. Provide `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` in metadata or as `data-pptx-x/y/width/height` on the group (complete explicit bounds are absolute slide coordinates; omitted bounds are inferred from the fallback geometry); JSON-first markers require all four in metadata. Classic charts accept a root `plot_area` rectangle inside the frame. Ranges, read-compatible spellings, and what the checker validates: [`native-data.md`](../scripts/docs/native-data.md).

```xml
<g id="p03-revenue-chart" data-pptx-replace-with="chart">
  <metadata type="application/json">
    {
      "x": 120, "y": 150, "width": 520, "height": 320,
      "name": "p03-revenue-chart",
      "type": "column",
      "title": "Revenue by Segment",
      "categories": ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3"],
      "series": [
        {"name": "Cloud", "values": [12, 15, 19]},
        {"name": "Services", "values": [8, 9, 11]}
      ]
    }
  </metadata>
  <!-- Visible SVG fallback for live preview / non-native export goes here. -->
</g>
```

**Hard rule — project by the selected authority**: SVG-first metadata describes the same data and visible chrome as its fallback — for a chart every category/point and series value (`null` for a break in a line), x/y/size data, visible point colors and markers (`line_style` / `point_colors`), line/area treatment (a line over a translucent fill is a `combo` of an area plot and a line plot), title/axis/legend chrome, companion text, bounds, and typography native export cannot infer; bar categories follow payload order top-down, and bar spacing, clustered overlap, and where a line starts inside `plot_area` are read from the fallback; for a table every resolved cell, header/summary line, rectangular span, cell style, alignment, bounds, and typography. JSON-first metadata is the authority and its preview may be approximate. Never simplify the artwork to fit the payload: when the closed payload cannot carry required data or topology, Default returns the native-ready decision upstream and Quick revises it before drawing; only the resolved non-native object stays unmarked, and an explicit `=yes` is never silently ignored. **Per-page verification**: every `=yes` key matches exactly one marker with one JSON child, and `=no` / unlisted objects have none — `rg -n 'data-pptx-replace-with="(chart|table)"|<metadata type="application/json">' <project_path>/svg_output/<current_page>.svg`.

### Table schema — `ppt-master.semantic-table.v2`

Every payload carries that exact `schema`; `columns` holds the optional header row and `rows` the body rows; `column_widths` / `row_heights` are relative weights. A cell is a string or an object with `text` (or `paragraphs` for rich text), `fill`, `color`, `align` (`l` / `ctr` / `r`), `valign` (`top` / `middle` / `bottom`), `bold`, `font_size`, `padding`, and per-side `borders` keyed `left` / `right` / `top` / `bottom` / `diagonal_down` / `diagonal_up` (full words, unlike `align`; each side is `{"style": "none"}` or `{"style": "solid", "color", "width"}`; a border without `style` is rejected); exact repetition may be factored into `defaults.cell` / `defaults.paragraph` / `defaults.run` (cell fields such as `align`, `valign`, `padding`, `font_size`, `borders` go under `defaults.cell`, never directly under `defaults`) and named `cell_styles`. Merged cells use positive `row_span` / `col_span` on the anchor with every covered cell as `{"merge_continuation": true}`. The complete field grammar: [`native-data.md`](../scripts/docs/native-data.md).

**Hard rule — the table payload is complete**: every row, summary line, value, and cell style that must survive `--native-charts-and-tables` is in `columns` / `rows`, because fallback text is discarded on that route. A payload holding only `font_size` and a uniform border is not complete when the fallback draws a header band, row or column fills, first-column emphasis, non-uniform row heights, or sparse rules. Numeric or currency columns use cell objects with `align: "r"` (`text-anchor="end"` does not carry).

### Chart schemas

Supported `type` values: `column`, `bar`, `line`, `area` (each with `grouping`), `pie`, `doughnut`, `pieOfPie`, `barOfPie`, `radar`, `radarMarkers`, `radarFilled`, `scatter`, `bubble`, `combo`, `treemap`, `sunburst`, `histogram`, `pareto`, `boxWhisker`, `waterfall`, `funnel`, `stock`. Category charts take `categories` plus `series[].values`; XY charts take `series[].x` / `y` (bubble adds `size`); combo takes `plots[]` or typed `series[]`; ChartEx types take their own hierarchy or value fields. `data_labels` (column / bar / line / area plots only; other types show values through companion text), `axes` (per axis `minimum` / `maximum` / `major_unit`, never `min` / `max`), `axis_titles`, `show_legend` / `legend_position`, companion text (`caption`, `source`, `note`), and `style.colors` are the chrome fields. 3D aliases and `surface` are unsupported; exploded pie, `map`, `heatmap`, `bullet`, and `gantt` fail fast. A PPTX import spells `pieOfPie` / `barOfPie` as `of_pie` plus `of_pie_type`; keep the imported spelling when editing, and note the second plot's split is not a JSON field. Every field, enum, and range: [`native-data.md`](../scripts/docs/native-data.md).

**Chart chrome and color**: SVG-first metadata matches the fallback chrome and reads it literally — the dominant stroke of elements named `axis` becomes `style.axis_color` and of those named `grid` becomes `style.grid_color` (unlabeled lines fall back to the marker's dominant stroke), numbers keep their written form (a payload `73.0` renders as `73` unless `number_format` says otherwise), and marker text that is not a category, data label, axis label, or legend entry needs a companion entry; JSON-first owns its chrome. Generated payloads use uppercase `#RRGGBB`. Negative bars keep the series fill. The final checker tags SVG-first parity findings `blocks --native-charts-and-tables export`; that export refuses them, so clear them before exporting the native variant.

**Forbidden — replacement marker transforms**: no rotate, skew, or matrix on table/chart groups; translate/scale only, because native frames cannot carry arbitrary SVG transforms.

1	> See [`shared-standards-core.md`](./shared-standards-core.md) for the mandatory SVG foundation.
2	
3	# SVG Effects and Geometry Specification
4	
5	Authority for advanced paint, effects, transforms, freeform/radial geometry, and constructed visual styles. Default and Quick Generate load it on the executor-base routing trigger — the first page whose visual job reaches beyond the everyday block — and keep it for the rest of the run; other SVG-authoring routes follow their workflow trigger. It keeps the form the model writes and the design decisions behind each technique; the complete grammar the checker and exporter enforce for §6.2–§6.10 is in [`svg-contract.md`](../scripts/docs/svg-contract.md) Part II under the same section numbers; §6.1 and §6.11–§6.13 are design guidance with no separate contract.
6	
7	**Cross-reference map**: unqualified §1, §2, and §4 references point to [`shared-standards-core.md`](./shared-standards-core.md); §6 references are local to this file.
8	
9	## 6. Advanced SVG Effects and Authoring Techniques
10	
11	**Mandatory**: once triggered, read this file completely before that page's
12	first SVG line and keep its compatible techniques in active construction vocabulary.
13	Before finalizing each page, run the §6.1 selection procedure, with the Visual
14	Job Router as recall for the jobs it diagnoses. Use §6.13 when diagnosed
15	jobs benefit from one coordinated page recipe.
16	
17	**Default — situational use (may override when plain construction is stronger)**:
18	“Advanced” means capability depth, not an effect quota. During page authoring,
19	recall relevant techniques from content, hierarchy, legibility, semantics,
20	rhythm, and style; apply those that materially help.
21	
22	### 6.1 Availability, Precedence, and Fidelity
23	
24	| Decision layer | Authority |
25	|---|---|
26	| Technical validity | Required / Forbidden / Conditional contracts in this file, over the shared core's closed authoring surface, the route's other required construction references, and any triggered module |
27	| Project values | Default: `<project_path>/spec_lock.md` anchors plus retained Design Spec/page context; Quick: anchors resolved in the current context |
28	| Aesthetic fit | Locked or Quick-resolved `visual_style` / `visual_style_behavior` |
29	| Per-page choice | Content purpose, hierarchy, legibility, semantics, and rhythm |
30	
31	**Reference — job-first effect selection**: establish the editable semantic
32	skeleton first; the Visual Job Router below lists the visual jobs an effect can
33	serve.
34	
35	| Pass | Decision |
36	|---|---|
37	| Skeleton / diagnose | Establish native information, relationships, and hierarchy. Image/text integration, plane separation, focus, state/direction, material/style, and the recurring motif are the jobs an effect can serve. |
38	| Surface / select | Name the target, confirm its owning subsection and fidelity, and let the Router recall candidates. Choose a compatible technique that fully performs the job; prefer simpler/native-stable alternatives only when communication is equal. `Approximate` requires review, not automatic rejection. |
39	| Integrate / stop | Align paint, contour, light, hierarchy, and z-order; combine only techniques with different jobs. Check legibility, editability, density, fidelity, and style; simplify failures, use legal alternatives, and bake only the smallest pixel-dependent layer. Keep authoritative text/data native. |
40	
41	**Reference — page-level recipes**: §6.13 carries a back-to-front layer stack for
42	cover, divider, text-led explanation, process, evidence, comparison, closing, and
43	cross-page motif pages. Read it with this router rather than after the page is
44	already composed.
45	
46	**Default — one dominant composition scaffold (may override when a second
47	scaffold performs an independent communication job)**: Integrate the page-scale
48	move and every active Structure / Image / Chart / Table branch into one dominant
49	system, sharing direction, contour, baseline, and z-order as applicable. Make a
50	branch-local system visibly subordinate when it cannot share that scaffold;
51	simplify any competing scaffold without a separate communication job.
52	
53	#### Visual Job Router
54	
55	**Reference — not a quota**: recall candidates for a diagnosed problem from
56	this table. A page may use no listed technique, one technique, or several
57	techniques with different jobs. The table recalls constructions rather than
58	bounding them: one it never names is equally valid when it satisfies every
59	applicable technical contract. Those contracts are the boundary; membership in
60	this table is not.
61	
62	| Diagnosed visual problem | Candidate technique | Authority / stop |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| Meaningful direction, continuous value, or center focus is missing | Linear/radial gradient or channel alpha | §6.2 / §6.3; otherwise keep solid paint |
65	| Picture/card/overlay elevation or boundary is unclear | Object or picture/carrier shadow, restrained glow, or hairline | §6.4; one light direction |
66	| Native copy and image do not integrate | Scrim, fade, wash, vignette, off-center spotlight, or faux glass | §6.5 and the Image-Treatment Implementation Map; verify contrast; no backdrop blur |
67	| Relationship state, direction, continuity, or boundary is unclear | Draft/optional/future → dash; direction → marker; undirected → solid; continuous flow → gradient stroke; repeated boundary → frame/contour/crop edge; exact grid → multi-subpath | §6.6 / §6.3; every line needs a job |
68	| Body copy carries a load-bearing figure, contrast, or noun that does not survive a scan | Inline emphasis run — a nested `<tspan>` with its own fill or weight inside the same paragraph | §6.7; the frame stays one editable text object |
69	| Short display text needs notation, silhouette, or material/image emphasis | Removed/former → strike; eyebrow distinction → tracking; display silhouette → outline/gradient; justified material/image emphasis → native picture/texture fill; luminous metric → glow; semantic list → native bullet | §6.7 / §6.3 / §6.4; no decorative body-copy treatment |
70	| Tilt, repetition, or reversible asset direction helps composition | Rotate, translate/mirror, or local `<use>` | §6.8; never mirror text, logos, or directional evidence |
71	| Resolved style needs hand, print, pixel, facets, layers, ribbon, or line-plus-area | Matching constructed recipe | §6.11; no generic decorative freeform |
72	| Meaning needs an unmatched silhouette, radial hierarchy, gauge, or custom route | Freeform, explicit arc/sector, or calculated arrowhead | §6.9 / §6.10; prefer an equal stock shape/marker |
73	| Look depends on dense texture, source blur, per-pixel composite, reflection, or skew | Native-safe alternative or prepared/baked asset | §6.12; text/data stay editable |
74	
75	#### Image-Treatment Implementation Map
76	
77	**Reference — not a constraint**: when image composition names one of these
78	modifier or prepared-asset treatments, resolve its implementation here.
79	`Effect-only` keeps a visible capability here without restoring a layout ID.
80	
81	| Image handles / treatment | Construction / boundary |
82	|---|---|
83	| `M2 · 01/03/04/08/09` · scrim, wash, fade, grid | Explicit solid/linear/radial layers over one picture; §6.2 / §6.3 / §6.5 |
84	| `M2 · 06/07` · atmospheric wash, watermark/receded field | Reduced picture alpha + optional wash; subordinate to native content; §6.2 / §6.5 |
85	| `M2 · 02/05` · vignette or spotlight | Radial layer with movable `fx/fy` or `cx/cy`; outer geometry `Approximate`; §6.3 / §6.5 |
86	| `M3 · 04` · lifted picture panel / visible overlay edge | Picture/carrier shadow, glow, or hairline; shadow one support shape for a framed/captioned panel; §6.4 |
87	| `M3 · 01/02/05` · frame, print frame, contour/cut edge | Registered native stroke/path; §6.6 |
88	| `M3 · 03; M1 · 09` · rotation, misregistration, Riso offset | Transform + explicit duplicate layers; §6.8 / §6.11 |
89	| `M1 · 03` + effect-only forms · paper cut, facets/folds, ribbon, staging | Ordered paths/facets + consistent paint/light; §6.11 / [`native-shape-authoring.md`](./native-shape-authoring.md) §7 |
90	| `M1 · 01/02/04–08` · crop, opening, subtraction, reveal | Direct clip or materialized Boolean; no `<mask>`; §1.2 / [`native-shape-authoring.md`](./native-shape-authoring.md) §6 |
91	| Effect-only · faux glass | Visible field + translucent panel + highlight; no blur or frosted-crop substitution; §6.5 |
92	| `A1 · 02–04; A3 · 02/03` · blur, duotone, blend, frost, desaturation | Prepared local bitmap/composite/derivative; registered frost is a blurred derivative; §6.12 |
93	
94	**Reference — illustrative colors**: colors below demonstrate syntax only;
95	generated pages choose paint from the Default locked or Quick-resolved identity
96	anchors, visual style, content semantics, and current composition. A contextual
97	tint, gradient stop, shadow/glow paint, or one-off display color need not
98	already be a persistent identity role; promote it only when it becomes a
99	recurring named role. Review an `Approximate` result in native PPTX when the
100	effect carries material meaning.
101	
102	---
103	
104	### 6.2 Color, Alpha, and Opacity
105	
106	Write solid paint as uppercase `#RRGGBB`, `none`, or an exact local `url(#id)`.
107	Put alpha on the channel that owns it — `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`,
108	`stop-opacity`, or `flood-opacity` as a unitless `0..1` — and use element
109	`opacity` only for an `<image>` or one non-group atomic object that fades all
110	of its channels together. Do not use element `opacity` as an alias for
111	`rgba()` on a fill-only object, and prefer descendant alpha over group opacity
112	(§2.2). Alpha multiplies down the tree: color alpha × ancestor group opacity ×
113	element opacity × channel opacity. Named colors, short/alpha HEX, `rgb()` /
114	`hsl()`, and percentages remain compatible input that the checker only
115	recommends normalizing.
116	
117	---
118	
119	### 6.3 Gradients and Paint Effects
120	
121	A gradient is a direct `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>` in `<defs>` with
122	≥2 explicit-color stops at non-decreasing `0..1` offsets, referenced by exact
123	`url(#id)`, in `objectBoundingBox` units — no `gradientTransform`,
124	`spreadMethod`, or CSS gradients. Linear exports as an angle
125	(`Native-normalized`); radial keeps only its focus point and normalizes the
126	outer circle to the object (`Approximate`), so place the hotspot with `fx/fy`
127	inside the object and expect the rim to differ. Text takes gradient fill only;
128	images take no gradient paint (use §6.5 overlays). A gradient *stroke* needs a
129	path with both width and height — a perfectly horizontal or vertical gradient
130	ribbon disappears, so author it as a closed gradient-filled band. Stop colors
131	are contextual paint: keep them coherent with the deck anchors and page
132	intent without duplicating a lock row.
133	
134	```xml
135	<defs>
136	  <linearGradient id="flow" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
137	    <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#2563EB"/>
138	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#10B981" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
139	  </linearGradient>
140	</defs>
141	<path d="M100 200 C260 80 420 320 620 180" fill="none"
142	      stroke="url(#flow)" stroke-width="12"/>
143	```
144	
145	**Native text picture/texture fill**: when the design calls for a photograph,
146	material, or texture inside editable glyphs, fill the `<text>` (or a
147	non-positional `<tspan>`) with a registered single-image `<pattern>` marked
148	`data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"` or `"tile"`. It exports as a PowerPoint
149	run picture fill (`stretch` `Native-normalized`; `tile` needs visual review),
150	not as a general SVG pattern; the text stays editable. The glyphs are the
151	only thing showing the image, so the fill must read as one value against the
152	ground — a near-uniform texture or material, not a scene, gradient, or
153	anything with its own light and dark regions, which breaks the letterforms
154	into unreadable patches (a 2026-09-10 cover title was lost this way).
155	
156	```xml
157	<defs>
158	  <pattern id="titleTexture" data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"
159	           patternUnits="objectBoundingBox"
160	           patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1">
161	    <image href="../images/cloud-texture.png"
162	           x="0" y="0" width="1" height="1"
163	           preserveAspectRatio="none"/>
164	  </pattern>
165	</defs>
166	<text x="96" y="220" fill="url(#titleTexture)" fill-opacity="0.85"
167	      font-family="Microsoft YaHei" font-size="72" font-weight="700">
168	  国风之美
169	</text>
170	```
171	
172	Preset patterns are a separate PPT interface in [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md).
173	
174	---
175	
176	### 6.4 Shadows, Glow, and Elevation
177	
178	A filter is native-effect metadata, not a pixel-filter surface: one direct
179	`<defs><filter>` referenced as a direct `filter="url(#id)"` on a `<rect>`,
180	`<circle>`, `<polygon>`, `<image>`, `<path>`, `<text>`, or a helper-authored preset group,
181	built from `feDropShadow` or the blur + flood + composite + merge graph below
182	with explicit `stdDeviation`, `dx`/`dy`, and `flood-opacity`. A meaningful
183	offset becomes one outer shadow; zero offset — even `feDropShadow` with
184	`dx="0" dy="0"` — becomes one glow. Both are `Approximate`: one filter, one
185	DrawingML effect. Filters on `<tspan>` or ordinary `<g>` and every other
186	primitive are forbidden; use an existing accent color for glow, since black
187	reads as diffuse shadow.
188	
189	```xml
190	<defs>
191	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
192	    <feDropShadow dx="0" dy="6" stdDeviation="8"
193	                  flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10"/>
194	  </filter>
195	  <filter id="expandedShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
196	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8" result="b"/>
197	    <feOffset in="b" dx="0" dy="6" result="o"/>
198	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10" result="c"/>
199	    <feComposite in="c" in2="o" operator="in" result="s"/>
200	    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="s"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
201	  </filter>
202	  <filter id="titleGlow" x="-30%" y="-30%" width="160%" height="160%">
203	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="b"/>
204	    <feFlood flood-color="#38BDF8" flood-opacity="0.45" result="c"/>
205	    <feComposite in="c" in2="b" operator="in" result="g"/>
206	    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="g"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
207	  </filter>
208	</defs>
209	```
210	
211	| Elevation | Use | `dy` | `stdDeviation` | Alpha |
212	|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
213	| Floor | Backgrounds, dividers, equal peers, body containers, decorative lines/icons, single-layer pages | — | — | — |
214	| Resting | Card over photo/panel, secondary callout | 2–4 | 4–8 | 0.06–0.10 |
215	| Raised | Primary CTA, focused card, overlay | 6–10 | 10–16 | 0.12–0.20 |
216	| Glow | Short display text, metric, focus accent | 0 offset | 4–8 | 0.35–0.55 |
217	
218	**Default — one light source per page (may override when every affected layer
219	uses one deliberate alternative direction)**: every `feOffset` shadow on one
220	slide shares the same `dx`/`dy` direction (default `dx="0"`,
221	`dy="4"`–`dy="8"`, light from upper front). Contradictory shadow directions
222	make one plane read as several incompatible surfaces. A deliberate upward
223	paper-layer treatment flips every affected layer together, so one plane keeps
224	one light direction.
225	
226	**Reference — not a constraint**: use no more elevation categories than the
227	hierarchy needs; a page may reuse one category across several related objects,
228	but two or three shadowed objects usually read cleanest — check that a fourth
229	earns its weight. Pick one weight tool per container — shadow, border,
230	gradient fill, or strong tint — never stacked; peer-grid cards, dividers,
231	body containers, and background panels stay on the floor.
232	Same-family colored shadow is reserved for a focal accent. On dark backgrounds
233	a light hairline or restrained glow separates surfaces; glow on body copy
234	reduces legibility. For older/strict renderers, replace a filter with two or
235	three offset translucent shapes behind the object: alpha `0.03–0.05`,
236	increasing offset/radius, and optional same-family tint near `0.04`
237	(`Native-stable`).

241	### 6.5 Image Treatments, Overlays, and Glass-like Surfaces
242	
243	| Need | Authoring contract | Fidelity |
244	|---|---|---|
245	| Cover/crop | Readable raster dimensions + aligned `slice` | Native `srcRect`; `Native-stable` |
246	| Contain/fit | Aligned `meet` | Fitted picture frame; `Native-normalized` |
247	| Stretch | `preserveAspectRatio="none"` | Native stretched frame |
248	| Uniform fade | `<image opacity="...">` | Native picture alpha |
249	| Shaped picture | §1.2 image-only `clip-path` | Preset/custom picture geometry |
250	
251	Every `<image>` has explicit positive `width`/`height`, one decodable
252	project-local or data-URI `href`, and — when not the default `xMidYMid meet` —
253	an aligned `preserveAspectRatio` with explicit `meet` or `slice`, or `none`
254	alone. A clip disables `meet` frame-fit, so match the box to the source ratio
255	or use `slice`; put a §6.4 filter directly on an unclipped image, and for a
256	clipped one on an exact outer `<g>` whose sole visual child is that image —
257	never both on the same `<image>`. A nested `<svg>` is only the exact
258	single-image crop wrapper the crop parser accepts, not a general viewport;
259	its required form (outer `preserveAspectRatio="none"` + `overflow="hidden"`
260	+ unit-space `viewBox`, child `<image>` at `0 0 1 1`) is in
261	[`svg-contract.md`](../scripts/docs/svg-contract.md) under "Nested SVG is
262	picture-crop transport".
263	
264	| Overlay | Construction | Typical stops / alpha |
265	|---|---|---|
266	| Directional scrim | Linear rect, darkest beside text | `0%: 0.88; 55%: 0.30; 100%: 0` |
267	| Bottom title fade | Vertical rect over lower image | black `0 → 0.72` |
268	| Vignette/spotlight | Radial rect; place the hotspot with `fx/fy` or `cx/cy` inside the canonical focus circle; outer center/radius remain approximate | black `0 → 0.58` |
269	| Brand wash | Directional existing brand-color gradient | `0.80 → 0.10` |
270	| Grid scrim | Seamless no-stroke rect cells over one image; vary neighboring alpha narrowly and irregularly | Keep the field subordinate; a regular alternation reads as a checkerboard |
271	| Faux glass | Visible fields + diagonal linear panel (`0,0 → 1,1`) + highlight stroke; optional §6.4 elevation | white `0.38 → 0.12`; stroke about `0.55` |
272	
273	Layer in document order: image → scrim/wash → text. True source/backdrop blur is
274	`Bake-required`; faux glass is explicit layering, not blur. Validate contrast
275	against the actual image. All overlay gradients follow §6.3 linear/radial
276	fidelity.

280	### 6.6 Lines, Connectors, Borders, and Markers
281	
282	A solid stroke with width and alpha is an editable native line. Dashes map to
283	the five presets (`4,4` / `6,3` dash, `2,2` sysDot, `8,4` lgDash, `8,4,2,4`
284	lgDashDot) or to one custom `dash gap` pair; caps are `butt` / `round` /
285	`square`, joins `miter` / `round` / `bevel`, `vector-effect` `none` or
286	`non-scaling-stroke`. Markers follow §1.1 (type native, size approximate); a
287	gradient stroke follows §6.3.
288	
289	**Default — relationship-fit dash rhythm (may override when style calls for
290	another rhythm)**: after §6.1 selects dash, preserve direction markers and
291	branch-owned placeholder patterns.
292	
293	| Already-dashed/dotted job (illustrative) | Dash |
294	|---|---|
295	| Separator/boundary | `4,4` |
296	| Subtle dotted border/generic non-image placeholder | `2,2` |
297	| Optional/future timeline/flow connector | `8,4` |
298	| Technical/dimension line | `8,4,2,4` |
299	
300	**Default — contour-fit joins (may override when the resolved style calls for
301	another character)**: smooth polyline/organic form → `round`; technical
302	diagram → `bevel`; crisp rectangle/arrow → `miter`.
303	
304	```xml
305	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12"
306	  fill="none" stroke="#999999" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
307	<line x1="100" y1="420" x2="500" y2="420"
308	  stroke="#1A73E8" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>
309	<polyline points="100,200 200,100 300,200" fill="none"
310	  stroke="#1A73E8" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
311	```
312	
313	Match marker paint to the parent stroke using the shape-specific channel from
314	§1.1: fill for closed/oval line ends and stroke for the open arrow. Use markers
315	for connectors and §6.10 calculated geometry for a manual diagonal arrowhead.
316	When exact grid spacing matters, use one multi-subpath path rather than a
317	fixed-density preset pattern:
318	
319	```xml
320	<path d="M40 0V120 M80 0V120 M0 40H120 M0 80H120"
321	      fill="none" stroke="#2E6EA8" stroke-width="0.8"/>
322	```

325	
326	### 6.7 Advanced Text Treatments
327	
328	Generated text uses only the canonical values: `font-weight` `normal` / `bold`
329	/ an integer hundred, `font-style` `normal` / `italic`, `text-anchor` on
330	`<text>` or above, `text-decoration` `underline` / `line-through` / both,
331	direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>`, and unitless-px
332	`letter-spacing` and `font-size`. Inheritable text declarations belong only on
333	`<svg>`, `<g>`, `<text>`, or `<tspan>`; `xml:space` (`default` or `preserve`) on
334	`<text>` / `<tspan>` is the one whitespace control — it inherits through the
335	text tree and may be reset on a child `<tspan>`, so one frame can mix
336	collapsed and preserved runs. Every other `font-*` / `text-*`
337	property has no native mapping and is an error.
338	
339	| Treatment | SVG surface | Result / boundary |
340	|---|---|---|
341	| Underline / strike / both | `text-decoration="underline"`, `line-through`, or both | `Native-stable`; both emits both run properties |
342	| Mixed runs | Non-positional `<tspan>` | One `Native-normalized` editable frame; §4.2 |
343	| Superscript / subscript | Direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>` | Editable run at PowerPoint's native baseline offset; set `font-size` on the same run when a smaller glyph is intended |
344	| Tracking | Unitless-px `letter-spacing` | `Native-normalized`; negative tracking must leave every run a positive advance |
345	| Transparency | `opacity` / `fill-opacity` on text/run | `Native-normalized` run alpha, not isolated compositing |
346	| Gradient fill | §6.3 gradient on text/run | Editable fill; geometry normalizes |
347	| Outline | Solid `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-opacity` | `Native-normalized` editable run outline; re-import does not reconstruct it |
348	| Shadow/glow | §6.4 filter on `<text>` only | Shape shadow / run glow; `Approximate` |
349	| Native bullet | Leading `· • ● ▪ ■ ◆ ◇ ◦ ‣` + non-empty content | `·`/`•` → `•`; others unchanged; color/alpha from marker run; font/size follow text |
350	
351	**Inline emphasis**: bold or accent-colored `<tspan>` runs lift numerical
352	results, explicit contrasts, or a load-bearing noun inside prose; green/red
353	conventionally read as polarity.
354	
355	```xml
356	<!-- Uniform: the two results disappear into the sentence. -->
357	<text x="80" y="200" font-size="20" fill="#333333">
358	  2024年公司营收同比增长35%达到12亿元创历史新高
359	</text>
360	
361	<!-- Lifted: data-bearing runs carry the scan. -->
362	<text x="80" y="200" font-size="20" fill="#333333">
363	  2024年公司营收同比<tspan fill="#1A73E8" font-weight="bold">增长35%</tspan>达到<tspan fill="#1A73E8" font-weight="bold">12亿元</tspan>创历史新高
364	</text>
365	```
366	
367	**Underline** conventionally marks links, key terms, or local emphasis —
368	decorate the linked run, not the whole sentence. **Strikethrough** marks
369	removed/former values; it is ordinary notation, not a style-exclusive effect.
370	
371	```xml
372	<text x="100" y="240" font-size="18" fill="#333333">Read <a
373	  href="https://example.com"><tspan text-decoration="underline">the guide</tspan></a>.</text>
374	<text x="100" y="200" font-size="20" xml:space="preserve">Current <tspan
375	  fill="#999999" text-decoration="line-through">old</tspan> value</text>
376	<text x="100" y="240" font-size="20">CO<tspan
377	  baseline-shift="sub" font-size="14">2</tspan></text>
378	```
379	
380	**Hard rule — generated decorative lettering ownership**: approved AI
381	decorative lettering is a prepared `<image>` asset under the image contracts,
382	not an advanced native-text treatment. Keep ordinary editable titles and
383	subtitles as normal `<text>`; this contract does not add WordArt, text warp, or
384	text-on-path authoring.
385	
386	CJK tracking defaults near/below 2% of font size and above 5% triggers review.
387	Text outline is solid only. `textPath`, masks, blend modes, generated effects,
388	and text-image knockouts are outside editable text.

392	### 6.8 Transforms, Layering, and Static Reuse
393	
394	Use only lowercase `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`, and `matrix` with finite
395	unitless arguments; `rotate` is clockwise and may take a pivot. Geometry,
396	images, and geometry-only groups accept any of them (`Native-normalized`) as
397	long as the cumulative matrix stays finite, non-zero, and orthogonal — no
398	`skewX` / `skewY` or shear, and `matrix` excludes rounded rectangles. Text, and
399	any group containing text, takes only a translate-only list or one rotate; set
400	text size/position directly. Native chart/table markers allow translate/scale
401	only. Mirror around a vertical pivot `cx` with
402	`translate(cx 0) scale(-1 1) translate(-cx 0)`, and never mirror text, logos,
403	or directional evidence.
404	
405	Layer back-to-front: background/image → scrim/shadow → main geometry → labels /
406	icons → top annotation; source order is PPT z-order. Local `<use>` (§1.3) is
407	compile-time reuse — finalization and native export expand it into cloned
408	editable primitives, and PowerPoint retains no symbol/instance graph. Group
409	opacity remains an approximate compatibility mapping; generated SVG prefers
410	descendant alpha (§2.2).
411	
412	---
413	
414	### 6.9 Freeform Shapes and Curves
415	
416	Every SVG path command, `<polygon>`, and `<polyline>` is accepted; export
417	normalizes to absolute `M/L` and cubic Béziers, and arcs become ≤90° cubic
418	segments (`Approximate`). Write `d` and `points` as finite unitless ordinary
419	decimals; geometry needs non-zero bounds; do not depend on
420	`fill-rule="evenodd"` — build explicit visible geometry, bake an essential
421	knockout, or on a fixed background use a background-colored overlay.
422	
423	**Reference — not a constraint**: use the fewest curve segments and control
424	points that preserve the intended silhouette. Set endpoints and tangent
425	directions first; use `S` after `C` or `T` after `Q` when reflected controls
426	preserve deliberate tangent continuity.
427	
428	```xml
429	<path d="M80 300 C180 180 300 180 400 300 S620 420 720 300"
430	      fill="none" stroke="#2563EB" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>
431	<path d="M80 520 Q240 400 400 520 T720 520"
432	      fill="none" stroke="#0F766E" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>
433	```
434	
435	Before authoring a freeform, apply [`native-shape-authoring.md`](./native-shape-authoring.md):
436	prefer editable primitives and exact Office presets, independently composed
437	when possible; materialize a Boolean only when one contour requires it. Use a
438	closed cubic path only for an organic silhouette those cannot express,
439	polygon/closed path for unmatched ribbons/facets, and an open path only for a
440	required data curve, custom route, or locked or Quick-resolved hand-drawn /
441	organic style. Straight relationships use `<line>`; exact stock bends/curves
442	use an authored native Connector preset. Multi-`M` paths remain available for
443	exact linework, and a §1.2 path clip for unmatched organic pictures. Filled
444	silhouettes end with `Z`; open paths use `fill="none"`. A rounded `<rect>`
445	stays a native adjustable `roundRect` only while `rx == ry` and the radius is at
446	most half the short side; unequal radii become custom geometry without a
447	handle.

450	
451	### 6.10 Radial Geometry, Donuts, Gauges, Sunbursts, and Diagonal Arrowheads
452	
453	For center `(cx,cy)`, radius `r`, and degrees `θ`:
454	
455	```text
456	x = cx + r × cos(θ × π / 180)
457	y = cy + r × sin(θ × π / 180)
458	```
459	
460	For clockwise pie/donut sectors, default to `-90°` only when the chart starts at
461	12 o'clock. A full-circle percentage sector spans `percentage × 360°`;
462	large-arc is `1` above `180°`; outer sweep is `1`, inner return is `0`. Split
463	both outer and inner boundaries of a full ring into at least two arcs each.
464	Verify all spans plus gaps against the planned sweep. Explicit arc sectors are
465	editable `Approximate` freeforms.
466	
467	```xml
468	<!-- 75% donut: center 400,400; outer 180; inner 100; -90° → 180°. -->
469	<path d="M400 220 A180 180 0 1 1 220 400
470	         L300 400 A100 100 0 1 0 400 300 Z" fill="#2563EB"/>
471	```
472	
473	**Gauge**: require `max > min`, `p = clamp((value-min)/(max-min),0,1)`, and
474	`0 < planned clockwise sweep <= 360°`; value sweep is `p × planned sweep`.
475	`valueEndAngle = startAngle + valueSweep`; large-arc is `1` iff
476	`abs(valueSweep) > 180°`. Omit the value sector at `p=0`. At `p=1` with
477	`360°`, split both boundaries into at least two arcs. Track/value share center,
478	radii, start, and sweep flags.
479	
480	**Sunburst — `Approximate`**: one explicit annular sector per node; each depth
481	owns one radius band and child angular intervals partition the parent. Do not
482	use one `evenodd` compound ring.
483	
484	A thin circle with a §6.6 preset or two-number dash stays a `Native-normalized`
485	ellipse line; the shorthand below is for thick ring segments only.
486	
487	**Thick-circle shorthand — `Approximate`, non-position-sensitive only**: one
488	`fill="none"` circle per segment with a two-value `dash gap` covering the
489	circumference and a direct `stroke-dashoffset`; native construction keeps only
490	the first dash and starts 90° counterclockwise from the SVG preview, so use
491	explicit arcs whenever start angle, cap, or radial precision matters.
492	
493	```xml
494	<circle cx="400" cy="400" r="140" fill="none" stroke="#2563EB"
495	        stroke-width="48" stroke-dasharray="615.75 263.90" stroke-dashoffset="0"/>
496	```
497	
498	**Diagonal polygon arrowhead**: for a non-zero line, calculate rather than use a
499	fixed triangle:
500	
501	```text
502	dx=x2-x1; dy=y2-y1; len=√(dx²+dy²); ux=dx/len; uy=dy/len
503	px=-uy; py=ux
504	tip=(x2,y2)
505	back1=(x2-ux×12+px×5, y2-uy×12+py×5)
506	back2=(x2-ux×12-px×5, y2-uy×12-py×5)
507	```
508	
509	Use §1.1 markers for ordinary connectors; the polygon is for a manually drawn
510	filled `Native-normalized` arrowhead. Example:
511	`<polygon points="370,430 365.6,417.8 358.2,424.6"/>`.
512

515	### 6.11 Constructed Technique Recipes
516	
517	**Hard rule — explicit construction**: these are supported-layer recipes, not
518	browser-filter permissions.
519	
520	**Reference — not a constraint**: use them only when they match the locked or
521	Quick-resolved style. Their curve recipes are explicit exceptions to the
522	Shape-first default above; they do not authorize decorative freeforms in
523	another style.
524	
525	| Family | Technique | Use when | Construction / boundary |
526	|---|---|---|---|
527	| Material / depth | Faux glass | Visible field must remain present behind a panel | §6.5 translucent panel + highlight; no backdrop blur; `Native-normalized` |
528	| Material / depth | Paper cut | Ordered layers/openings carry the material language | Organic paths + one §6.4 shadow per layer, never the group; `Approximate` |
529	| Hand / print | Hand-drawn mark | Annotation, underline, or highlighter gesture | Rotated translucent bar + restrained `Q/C` paths + round caps; no roughness filter; `Native-normalized` |
530	| Hand / print | Ink wash | Brush mass or atmosphere | Same-family translucent curves/strokes; no feather/wet edge; `Native-normalized` |
531	| Hand / print | Riso offset | Deliberate print misregistration | Offset duplicate, second ink, lower alpha; no blend mode; `Native-normalized` |
532	| Hand / print | Pixel grid | Sparse hard-cell digital accent | Integer-aligned rect grid; `shape-rendering` preview-only; `Native-stable` |
533	| Hand / print | Halftone | Sparse screen modulation | Calculated circles; `Native-stable`; bake dense screens or use [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md) |
534	| Form / geometry | Faceted or folded form | Isometric object, folded ribbon, dimensional numeral/band | Shared vertices, one light direction, same-hue alternating paint per [`native-shape-authoring.md`](./native-shape-authoring.md) §7.1; no 3D; `Native-normalized` |
535	| Form / geometry | Gradient ribbon | Continuous directional energy, not faceted depth | Cubic gradient stroke or closed gradient-filled band; no mesh gradient; `Native-normalized`, re-import may flatten color |
536	| Data expression | Line plus area | Magnitude context beneath an exact reading edge | Subordinate low-alpha area first, crisp line above; `Native-normalized` |
537	
538	**Minimal construction anchors**:
539	
540	```xml
541	<!-- Hand-drawn + ink. -->
542	<rect x="80" y="80" width="240" height="28" fill="#FDE68A"
543	      opacity="0.72" transform="rotate(-1,200,94)"/>
544	<path d="M90 150 Q210 142 330 151" fill="none" stroke="#1F2937"
545	      stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>
546	<path d="M80 220 C160 160 250 180 330 230 Z" fill="#1F2937" opacity="0.16"/>
547	<path d="M90 240 C180 210 250 260 340 220" fill="none" stroke="#1F2937"
548	      stroke-width="10" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.70"/>
549	
550	<!-- Riso, pixel cells, sparse dots. -->
551	<text x="86" y="320" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="64"
552	      fill="#EC4899" opacity="0.85">PRINT</text>
553	<text x="92" y="326" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="64"
554	      fill="#2563EB">PRINT</text>
555	<g id="pixel-cells" shape-rendering="crispEdges" fill="#2563EB">
556	  <rect x="400" y="80" width="16" height="16"/><rect x="416" y="80" width="16" height="16"/>
557	</g>
558	<g id="sparse-dots" fill="#EC4899"><circle cx="410" cy="140" r="3"/><circle cx="426" cy="140" r="6"/></g>
559	
560	<!-- Isometric facets + line-over-area. -->
561	<g id="isometric-facets" transform="translate(520 160)">
562	  <polygon points="0,0 80,-24 160,0 80,24" fill="#60A5FA"/>
563	  <polygon points="0,0 0,48 80,72 80,24" fill="#3B82F6"/>
564	  <polygon points="80,24 80,72 160,48 160,0" fill="#2563EB"/>
565	</g>
566	<path d="M760 260 L860 220 L960 250 L960 340 L760 340 Z" fill="#2563EB" opacity="0.10"/>
567	<path d="M760 260 L860 220 L960 250" fill="none" stroke="#2563EB" stroke-width="4"/>

571	treatment)**: avoid soft scaling; use explicit dots only for sparse editable
572	halftone and route dense full-slide texture to §6.12.

576	### 6.12 Unsupported Effects and Native-Safe Alternatives
577	
578	| Unsupported intent | Do not author | Fidelity | Alternative |
579	|---|---|---|---|
580	| Source/backdrop blur; procedural texture | Plain blur, `feTurbulence`, `feDisplacementMap`, `feColorMatrix`, arbitrary filter graph | `Bake-required` | §6.4 effect, explicit geometry, translucent layers, or baked texture |
581	| Inner shadow, soft edge, reflection | Non-outer-shadow/glow graph | `Bake-required` | Explicit inset/highlight/shadow layers or image |
582	| Per-pixel compositing | Mask, blend mode, knockout, arbitrary alpha composite | `Bake-required` | Direct geometry; §1.2 image clip; otherwise bake |
583	| Exact custom tile | Unannotated `<pattern>` / `patternTransform` | `Bake-required` | Multi-subpath geometry, suitable [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md) preset, or bake |
584	| Sheared object | Skew/shear matrix | `Bake-required` | Pre-transform geometry path; bake text/image |
585	
586	**Hard rule — blur semantics**: within §6.4, zero-offset `feGaussianBlur` means
587	glow; it does not blur the object or backdrop. Use a low-alpha raster for dense
588	grain and explicit circles/paths only for sparse editable marks.

592	### 6.13 Page-Level Composition Recipes
593	
594	**Reference — not a quota**: use the planned page skeleton; when images are
595	active, select it through
596	[`image-layout-patterns.md`](./image-layout-patterns.md). Read each recipe
597	back-to-front and omit every layer without a distinct job.
598	
599	| Page / deck job | Back-to-front stack | Stop |
600	|---|---|---|
601	| Cover | Hero field → optional scrim/wash → purposeful opening/contour → native title, optionally paired with a prepared decorative-lettering image | Stop when copy is safe and title/field read together |
602	| Divider | Image band or quiet field → restrained wash → recurring geometry → number/title | Reuse deck language |
603	| Text-led explanation | Quiet field → recurring material/contour → native hierarchy → optional local emphasis | Emphasis sits on the argument's load-bearing runs |
604	| Process / system | Context field → native relation lines → nodes/labels → optional state/direction focus | Every connector stays semantic |
605	| Evidence / metric | Context field → local contrast → native leaders/labels/metric → optional focus/elevation | Claims stay native |
606	| Comparison | Matched planes → optional shared wash/divider → matched labels → one difference marker | Keep crop, elevation, and paint symmetric unless asymmetry is the claim |
607	| Closing / CTA | Receded field → echoed contour/gradient → native action → optional raised accent | Keep the native action legible |
608	| Cross-page motif | Reuse contour, gradient direction, line language, texture, or light logic; vary scale, crop, position by page job | Preserve recognition without copying the page or adding novelty effects |
609	
610	---
